Dear [CONSUMER NAME],

Re: Dispute of Collection Account ACC-105814

We acknowledge receipt of your dispute regarding the collection account ACC-105814, which is currently reported to the credit bureaus. We understand that you have requested validation of this debt and disputed the accuracy of the reporting.

Pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA), we are required to provide you with a written validation notice within five days of receiving your dispute. We will investigate your dispute and provide a written validation notice, which will include the name and address of the original creditor, the amount of the debt, and a statement that unless you dispute the validity of this debt, we will assume it is valid.

We will also investigate the accuracy of the reporting and take any necessary steps to correct any errors.

Please note that we have a current balance of $4524.94 on this account, which was originally associated with Meridian Federal Credit Union. The account was charged off on November 26, 2023, and the last payment was received on April 13, 2023.

You have the right to dispute this debt further, and we will respond to any additional information you provide.

Sincerely,

[AGENCY NAME]

cc: Credit Bureaus

Note: This letter is not a validation notice, but rather a response to the consumer's dispute. A validation notice would be sent separately, as required by the FDCPA.
